title.value: Inference-Aware Fine-Tuning for Best-of-N Sampling in Large Language Models
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning and end of the paper.
title.quote: Inference-Aware Fine-Tuning for Best-of-N Sampling in Large Language Models

analysis.description: The paper introduces a novel inference-aware fine-tuning paradigm for large language models, focusing on optimizing inference strategies during training. It studies this paradigm using the Best-of-N (BoN) inference strategy and proposes imitation learning and reinforcement learning methods for BoN-aware fine-tuning, demonstrating improvements in performance and inference-time compute.

type.justification: The study involves empirical demonstrations and experiments demonstrating the effectiveness of BoN-aware fine-tuning on performance metrics.
type.quote: We empirically demonstrate that our BoN-aware models implicitly learn a meta-strategy that interleaves best responses with more diverse responses...Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of BoN-aware fine-tuning...

name.justification: The paper focuses on fine-tuning and inference strategies in large language models, which falls under Natural Language Processing.
name.quote: Recent studies have indicated that effectively utilizing inference-time compute is crucial for attaining better performance from large language models (LLMs).

name.justification: The paper discusses the use of reinforcement learning methods for BoN-aware fine-tuning.
name.quote: We develop a BoN-aware supervised fine-tuning algorithm...We extend our method to a general BoN-aware RL framework, enabling the policy to learn and solve downstream tasks under the BoN inference strategy.

name.justification: The core focus of the paper is on a novel fine-tuning paradigm for improving model performance during inference.
name.quote: In this work, we propose a novel inference-aware fine-tuning paradigm, in which the model is fine-tuned in a manner that directly optimizes the performance of the inference-time strategy.

name.justification: The paper specifically addresses improvements in the context of large language models.
name.quote: Our work makes several key contributions to the understanding and optimization of batch-of-neighbors (BoN) inference.

name.justification: Gemma 2B is mentioned as the model used in the experiments to demonstrate improvements using the proposed BoN-aware fine-tuning methods.
name.quote: Particularly, we show that our methods improve the Bo32 performance of Gemma 2B on Hendrycks MATH from 26.8% to 30.8%, and pass@32 from 60.0% to 67.0%, as well as the pass@16 on HumanEval from 61.6% to 67.1%.
